Refining 3DGS with AI: image versus video input for camera orbits

A Shibuya test separating photographic still quality from geometric consistency in motion.

I am Kou from Locahun3D. Compare photographic still refinement, Kling animation, and orbiting video in that order. View each output on its own before the side-by-side comparison.

Contents

  1. Refine still images
  2. Animate with Kling
  3. Compare orbiting videos
  4. Toward a compositing plate

Prices are US-dollar equivalents at Runway’s purchased-credit rate, excluding subscription, capture, labour and electricity. No additional credits were purchased.

Conversion basis: US$0.01 per credit

01 Refine still images

Use the same 3DGS render and prompt for a sunny midday architectural photograph. Output aspect-ratio settings differ.

Shared input

Target reference: GPT

Nano Banana Pro

Seedream 5.0 Pro

Nano produces brighter photographic materials; Seedream keeps framing closer to the source but retains darkness and scan artifacts. Both alter details. These examples do not establish an overall model ranking.

Side-by-side still comparison

02 Animate with Kling

Supply the two refined images to Kling 3.0 Pro with the same three-second forward-move prompt. The Seedream image is centre-cropped to 16:9.

From the Nano Banana image

From the Seedream image

Photographic appearance carries through, but both add advertising or people to originally black panels. Neither passes exact location-detail preservation.

Side-by-side review

03 Compare orbiting videos

The source is a Full HD, three-second, six-degree orbit rendered with Blender’s LCC2_DIRECT prototype, using captured colour without added lighting. This camera and input differ from the preceding chapters.

Wan 3.0

Compare first-frame-only and video-reference inputs with the same prompt, Full HD and three-second duration.

First frame only

3DGS video reference

Seedance 2.5

Use the same 3DGS video and prompt at Full HD for four seconds, with and without an auxiliary image. Request the source move over the first three seconds and a final one-second hold.

Auxiliary image

3DGS video only

3DGS video + Seedream reference

Even with the image, small lettering and window grids change, and another STARBUCKS wordmark appears on the right. Exact lettering and geometry preservation remain unmet.

Compare Wan and Seedance

This workflow comparison also changes the prompt, auxiliary input and requested duration. Seedance with the image gives stronger sunny lighting and materials in this pair, not a controlled ranking of the models alone.

Camera and geometry fidelity

The generated cameras do not match exactly. The models receive reference frames, not hard constraints for Blender position, rotation and focal length. Equal playback times do not guarantee equal viewpoints. Sign restoration through compositing and exact camera matching have not been demonstrated.

Unique results shown total US$10.62 equivalent, or US$12.27 including the excluded US$1.65 Edit attempt. Reused clips are not counted twice; the earlier GPT image and previous tests outside this article are excluded.

Seedance conditions and cost

Each condition was generated once. Repeatability and larger rotations remain untested. Both originals are 1920×1080, 24fps and approximately four seconds, without AI upscaling or colour correction. The Wan comparison edit selects frames from 30fps to 24fps and trims to three seconds. The reference image reduced the balance by nine credits and each Full HD clip used 374: 757 credits for this comparison stage. An earlier Edit-mode attempt returned 720p and approximately four seconds, was excluded from the Full HD comparison, and used a separate 165 credits. No additional credits were purchased. Nano Banana did not reach generation acceptance in this interface; Seedream supplied the image reference.

Comparison conditions and credits

All generations used Runway. The two stills reduced the displayed balance by 29 credits; the two Kling clips used 72; the two Wan orbit clips used 120. Seedream's displayed balance change differed from its listed price, so 29 is reported as the observed combined balance change. Side-by-side videos are edited comparison layouts, without AI upscaling or colour correction. The 3DGS source is 24fps and Wan outputs are 30fps; only the comparison edit matches frame rate through frame duplication or selection. See the official Runway pricing for current rates.

04 Combine a refined image and 3DGS for a compositing plate

Use Seedream to establish the desired appearance and 3DGS video to supply composition and motion. This pair improved materials and poster retention in our test, but faithful reproduction is not yet guaranteed. Treat appearance and camera, lettering and geometry preservation as separate tasks.

Seedance remains a candidate

Seedance with the Seedream reference improved sunny materials and poster retention. Small lettering and window grids changed, and an extra wordmark appeared, so it did not pass exact location preservation. Its image-plus-video cost was US$3.83 equivalent for about four seconds, versus US$0.93 for the three-second Aleph workflow. Different conditions prevent a definitive quality ranking.

Remaining camera and lighting limitations

Video reference does not lock the generated camera or geometry. Strict compositing requires checking every frame against the original-camera render. Full HD output also does not guarantee sharp lettering or window detail.

Establish sun direction, shadow softness and exposure, then match the reference image and added CG. Captured shadows remain baked into 3DGS colour; adding lights does not remove them. Free relighting and CG contact/shadow compositing were not tested here.

Generated result: Seedream + Aleph 2.0

The custom Seedream first frame was propagated through the original 3DGS clip with Aleph 2.0 Edit Studio. The original download is 1920×1080, 24fps and 72 frames. No AI upscale or colour correction was applied.

Daylight appearance and the large DMM poster carry through. Small lettering, poster faces and road details are still reconstructed. The orbit broadly follows the source, but exact camera and geometry matching have not been established. This is a generated background candidate, not an approved final compositing plate. Lettering and geometry repair and an actual CG contact/shadow test remain necessary for production use.

Generation and cost

Unlimited mode did not support this generation on the account. Switching to existing Credits enabled generation; no purchase was made. The balance decreased by 84 credits, equivalent to US$0.84. The US$0.09 reference was reused and counted only once in the article total.
